details: picklescan before 0.0.22 only considers standard pickle file extensions in the scope for its vulnerability scan. An attacker could craft a malicious model that uses Pickle and include a malicious pickle file with a non-standard file extension. Because the malicious pickle file inclusion is not considered as part of the scope of picklescan, the file would pass security checks and appear to be safe, when it could instead prove to be problematic.

A vulnerability in the GraphCypherQAChain class of langchain-ai/langchain-community version 0.2.5 allows for SQL injection through prompt injection. This vulnerability can lead to unauthorized data manipulation, data exfiltration, denial of service (DoS) by deleting all data, breaches in multi-tenant security environments, and data integrity issues. Attackers can create, update, or delete nodes and relationships without proper authorization, extract sensitive data, disrupt services, access data across different tenants, and compromise the integrity of the database.

descriptions.value: @fastify/session is a session plugin for Fastify. In all releases before 11.1.6, with the default rolling session behavior, a request that restored a session before a logout could save its own copy after another request had completed the session destroy call, recreating the destroyed session identifier with its authenticated data. An attacker who already holds a victim's valid signed session cookie and keeps a request in flight across the logout can replay that cookie to restore the session after it was meant to be revoked, without any cookie theft or signature forgery. The issue is fixed in @fastify/session 11.1.6, which adds a per session generation marker and a conditional store write so a session restored before a logout or regeneration cannot recreate or overwrite the current entry, and users should upgrade to 11.1.6 or later. There is no workaround, and custom session stores must implement the new conditional write.

cna.title: ZLMediaKit downloadFile Root-Directory Confinement Bypass via Prefix Collision

descriptions.value: ZLMediaKit confines the downloadFile API to a configured set of root directories with a prefix comparison that does not account for directory boundaries. The configuration loader in server/WebApi.cpp builds each root with File::absolutePath("", item, true); because the relative-path argument is empty that helper returns the value without a trailing separator. The handler then accepts a requested path when start_with(file_path, root) holds, so a sibling directory whose name merely begins with the configured root string satisfies the test and is served. The only other guard rejects a path containing two dots, which this requires none of. The equivalent confinement check for the ordinary static file server in src/Http/HttpFileManager.cpp computes its root with a non-empty second argument, which appends the separator before comparing, and so is not affected. The endpoint requires the configured API secret, so this grants no privilege beyond what that secret already implies, but it reads files outside the directory the operator confined it to, and the reference container runs the server as root.

descriptions.description: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal')

references.name: VulnCheck Advisory: ZLMediaKit downloadFile Root-Directory Confinement Bypass via Prefix Collision

cna.title: OpenPanel report.list Queries Reports by an Unverified dashboardId, Crossing Organization Boundaries

descriptions.value: The report.list procedure in packages/trpc/src/routers/report.ts accepted a projectId and a dashboardId and returned getReportsByDashboardId(dashboardId). The enforceAccess middleware in packages/trpc/src/trpc.ts verified membership for the supplied projectId, but nothing verified that the supplied dashboardId belonged to that project, and getReportsByDashboardId in packages/db/src/services/reports.service.ts selects reports by dashboardId alone with no project scoping. An authenticated user could therefore pair a projectId from their own organization, which satisfies the middleware, with a dashboardId belonging to another organization and receive every report in that dashboard. A correctly scoped helper, listReportsCore, already existed in the same service file and resolves the dashboard through getDashboardById(dashboardId, projectId) before returning reports, but the router did not use it.

references.name: VulnCheck Advisory: OpenPanel report.list Queries Reports by an Unverified dashboardId, Crossing Organization Boundaries

cna.title: OpenPanel report.get Returns Any Report by Identifier Without Checking Project Access

descriptions.value: The report.get procedure in packages/trpc/src/routers/report.ts accepted only a reportId and returned getReportById(reportId) directly. The enforceAccess middleware in packages/trpc/src/trpc.ts evaluates membership only when the input carries a projectId or organizationId key, so an input consisting of a reportId alone passed through unchecked, and getReportById in packages/db/src/services/reports.service.ts performs a findUnique on the report id with no project scoping. Any authenticated user could therefore read the full configuration of any saved report on the instance, including the owning projectId, event series, filters, breakdowns and formulas, by supplying its identifier. The adjacent update, delete and duplicate procedures resolve the report first and check getProjectAccess against the report's own projectId, so the omission was specific to this procedure.

references.name: VulnCheck Advisory: OpenPanel report.get Returns Any Report by Identifier Without Checking Project Access

cna.title: svg-sanitizer 0.11.0 before 1.1.0 Uncaught LogicException DoS via sanitize()

descriptions.value: svg-sanitizer from 0.11.0 before 1.1.0 contains an uncaught exception vulnerability that allows attackers to crash callers by submitting well-formed XML without a top-level svg root. Attackers can supply documents with a non-svg root or nested svg element, causing Sanitizer::sanitize() to throw a LogicException instead of returning false, crashing workers or bypassing upload rejection.

references.name: VulnCheck Advisory: svg-sanitizer 0.11.0 before 1.1.0 Uncaught LogicException DoS via sanitize()

cna.title: svg-sanitizer before 1.1.0 Quadratic CPU-Exhaustion DoS via PHP-Tag Stripping Loop

descriptions.value: svg-sanitizer from 0.5.3 before 1.1.0 contains a denial of service vulnerability in Sanitizer::sanitize() that repeatedly rescans the whole input while stripping PHP tags. Unauthenticated attackers can upload SVGs with many overlapping PHP tag openers and closers, forcing quadratic preg_replace passes that exhaust worker CPU for minutes.

references.name: VulnCheck Advisory: svg-sanitizer before 1.1.0 Quadratic CPU-Exhaustion DoS via PHP-Tag Stripping Loop

cna.title: darylldoyle svg-sanitizer before 1.0.0 CSS Injection and Remote Reference Bypass

descriptions.value: darylldoyle svg-sanitizer before 1.0.0 contains CSS injection and remote reference bypass vulnerabilities that allow attackers to embed external resources by uploading crafted SVG files. Attackers can use unsanitized style content, unquoted url() values, or image href attributes to exfiltrate page data, track users, or disclose visitor IP addresses.

descriptions.description: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting')

Attackers can lure an authenticated backend user to a crafted link containing a valid CSRF token, executing JavaScript that performs same-origin actions or reads DOM data.

descriptions.description: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting')

Attackers can craft a link with a valid CSRF token and HTML payload that rex_view::message() renders unescaped, executing scripts in a victim's backend session.

cna.title: REDAXO before 5.21.3 CSRF Token Bypass via users/users Privilege Escalation

descriptions.value: REDAXO before 5.21.3 contains a cross-site request forgery vulnerability in the backend user administration page (users/users) because the CSRF token check only runs when the save parameter is set, while the update path triggered by FUNC_UPDATE does not require it. Attackers can lure a logged-in backend user with the users[] permission to a crafted GET link to grant administrator rights, deactivate accounts, or lock out the sole administrator.

references.name: VulnCheck Advisory: REDAXO before 5.21.3 CSRF Token Bypass via users/users Privilege Escalation

cna.title: REDAXO before 5.21.3 Reflected XSS via opener_link in Media Pool

descriptions.value: REDAXO before 5.21.3 contains a reflected cross-site scripting vulnerability in the backend media pool detail page, where the opener_link parameter is rendered without HTML escaping. Unauthenticated attackers can lure logged-in backend users with media permissions into clicking a crafted link. The injected script can then read the CSRF token and perform actions with the victim's permissions, including code execution via template or module edits when the victim is an administrator.

descriptions.description: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting')

references.name: VulnCheck Advisory: REDAXO before 5.21.3 Reflected XSS via opener_link in Media Pool

cna.title: REDAXO before 5.21.3 CSRF in Article History Plugin

descriptions.value: REDAXO before 5.21.3 contains a cross-site request forgery vulnerability in the structure/history plugin that allows attackers to delete history or roll back content via unvalidated GET requests. Attackers can lure logged-in backend users to a page triggering func=clearall or rex_history_function=snap, permanently deleting all article snapshots or reverting articles to earlier states.

references.name: VulnCheck Advisory: REDAXO before 5.21.3 CSRF in Article History Plugin

cna.title: REDAXO 5.18.0 before 5.21.4 Stored XSS via Unsanitized Mediapool SVG Uploads

descriptions.value: REDAXO from 5.18.0 before 5.21.4 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability because rex_media_service moves uploaded SVG files into the public media folder before sanitizing them. Authenticated users with mediapool upload rights can race the sanitizer or exhaust memory limits to leave script-laden SVGs publicly served, executing scripts in victims' backend sessions.

descriptions.description: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting')

references.name: VulnCheck Advisory: REDAXO 5.18.0 before 5.21.4 Stored XSS via Unsanitized Mediapool SVG Uploads

cna.title: REDAXO Core 5.3.0 before 5.21.4 Authentication Bypass via History Plugin

descriptions.value: REDAXO core from 5.3.0 before 5.21.4 contains an authentication bypass vulnerability in the structure/history plugin that allows unauthenticated attackers to forge temporary login tokens. Attackers can force the session-tied secret into a predictable state and forge tokens for accounts like admin, gaining backend access and code execution outside live mode.

references.name: VulnCheck Advisory: REDAXO Core 5.3.0 before 5.21.4 Authentication Bypass via History Plugin

descriptions.description: CWE-532: Information Exposure Through Log Files

descriptions.value: In affected versions of Octopus Server, creating a user invitation writes the invitation code to the audit event log. When the invitation is linked to a space, a user in that space with appropriate permissions could read the code from the audit event. Successfully exploiting this by redeeming the unclaimed invitation could allow the user to escalate privileges however this is dependant on the permissions assigned for the invited user.

cna.title: REDAXO before 5.21.4 Stored XSS via Media and Link Input Widgets

descriptions.value: REDAXO before 5.21.4 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows content editors to inject HTML by storing unescaped values rendered by media, medialist, link and linklist widgets. Attackers can submit crafted REX_INPUT_MEDIA or REX_INPUT_LINK values that break out of the value attribute, executing script in administrators' backend sessions to hijack accounts.

cna.title: REDAXO before 5.21.4 Broken Access Control in Slice Operations

descriptions.value: REDAXO before 5.21.4 contains a broken access control vulnerability that allows authenticated editors to modify slices in unauthorized categories by pairing a permitted article with a foreign slice id. Attackers can abuse content/edit delete and edit functions or the content_slice_status and content_move_slice APIs to delete, toggle, move, or overwrite other editors' slices.

references.name: VulnCheck Advisory: REDAXO before 5.21.4 Broken Access Control in Slice Operations

cna.title: REDAXO before 5.21.4 Missing Authorization in Media Pool Bulk Move

descriptions.value: REDAXO before 5.21.4 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in the media pool bulk move that checks only target category permission, ignoring the source category. Authenticated backend users with permission for one media category can move files from restricted categories into it, then silently replace their contents site-wide.

references.name: VulnCheck Advisory: REDAXO before 5.21.4 Missing Authorization in Media Pool Bulk Move

cna.title: REDAXO before 5.21.4 Missing Authorization in Version and History Previews

descriptions.value: REDAXO core before 5.21.4 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in the structure/version and structure/history frontend preview modes, which do not check category or clang permissions for the previewed article. Any backend user, or one holding history[article_rollback], can set rex_version or rex_history_date with arbitrary article_id values to read unpublished working versions and historic or deleted content.

references.name: VulnCheck Advisory: REDAXO before 5.21.4 Missing Authorization in Version and History Previews

cna.title: REDAXO before 5.21.5 Privilege Escalation via Backup Export of Authentication Tables

descriptions.value: REDAXO before 5.21.5 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in the backup addon export that accepts any database table, allowing non-admin users with the backup[export] permission to export rex_user, rex_user_session, and other applications' tables. Attackers can obtain plaintext session ids and stay-logged-in keys to take over admin accounts, or password hashes for offline cracking.

references.name: VulnCheck Advisory: REDAXO before 5.21.5 Privilege Escalation via Backup Export of Authentication Tables

cna.title: REDAXO before 5.21.5 CSRF via Safe Mode Toggle Parameter

descriptions.value: REDAXO before 5.21.5 contains a cross-site request forgery vulnerability because the backend processes the safemode GET parameter in index.php without validating a CSRF token. Attackers can lure a logged-in administrator into opening a crafted link to disable global safe mode, writing safe_mode: false to config.yml, or enable session safe mode, disabling backend addons.

references.name: VulnCheck Advisory: REDAXO before 5.21.5 CSRF via Safe Mode Toggle Parameter

cna.title: REDAXO before 5.21.5 Insufficient Session Expiration on Password Change

descriptions.value: REDAXO before 5.21.5 contains an insufficient session expiration vulnerability that allows attackers to retain account access by keeping the current session and stay-logged-in key valid after a password change. Attackers who obtained a user's session id or stay-logged-in cookie can keep backend access after the password change, via the cookie for up to three months.

references.name: VulnCheck Advisory: REDAXO before 5.21.5 Insufficient Session Expiration on Password Change

cna.title: REDAXO core before 5.21.5 Missing Authorization in rex_api_package API

descriptions.value: REDAXO core before 5.21.5 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in the rex_api_package API function that lets non-admin backend users manage packages with only a valid CSRF token. Attackers holding a token, such as demoted admins with active sessions, can uninstall system addons like structure (dropping their database tables), deactivate, install, or activate packages, and delete non-system packages.

references.name: VulnCheck Advisory: REDAXO core before 5.21.5 Missing Authorization in rex_api_package API
